ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A square can be divided into four congruent figures as shown. For how many $n$ with $1 \le n \le 100$ can a unit square be divided into $n$ congruent figures?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: I inspected the attached image(s). The figure shows a square whose outer boundary is divided by one vertical line segment and one horizontal line segment through the square, forming a 2 by 2 grid of four congruent smaller squares. Reasoning: The question asks for how many integers n with 1 <= n <= 100 a unit square can be divided into n congruent figures. For any positive integer n, a unit square can be divided into n congruent vertical rectangles by making n - 1 equally spaced vertical cuts. Each rectangle has dimensions 1/n by 1, so all n pieces are congruent. Therefore every integer from 1 through 100 works, giving 100 possible values of n.
